title: The Covenant Renewed in Moab

questions.question: Did the clothes or sandals wear out in the 40 years?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:5 (ESV): "I have led you forty years in the wilderness. Your clothes have not worn out... and your sandals have not worn off..."

questions.question: What determines entry into this sworn covenant today?
options: All of you stand today before the Lord (leaders, men, women, children, sojourners)
questions.correctAnswer: All of you stand today before the Lord (leaders, men, women, children, sojourners)
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:10–11 (ESV): "You stand today, all of you, before the Lord... your little ones, your wives, and the sojourner..."

questions.question: What happens to the man who hears the curse but blesses himself in his heart?
options: The Lord will not be willing to forgive him; His anger will smoke against him
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord will not be willing to forgive him; His anger will smoke against him
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:19–20 (ESV): "...The Lord will not be willing to forgive him, but rather the anger of the Lord... will smoke against that man..."

questions.question: What will the generation to come say when they see the plagues of the land?
options: Why has the Lord done thus to this land? What caused this great anger?
questions.correctAnswer: Why has the Lord done thus to this land? What caused this great anger?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:24 (ESV): "...all the nations will say, 'Why has the Lord done thus to this land? What caused the heat of this great anger?'"

questions.question: To whom do the secret things belong?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:29 (ESV): "The secret things belong to the Lord our God..."

questions.question: To whom do the things that are revealed belong?
options: To us and to our children forever
questions.correctAnswer: To us and to our children forever
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:29 (ESV): "...but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children forever..."

questions.question: Why perform "all the words of this law"?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:29 (ESV): "...that we may do all the words of this law."

questions.question: What cities are mentioned as examples of overthrow?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:23 (ESV): "...like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim..."

questions.question: Why did the Lord uproot them?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:25 (ESV): "It is because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord..."

questions.question: What is described as a "root bearing poisonous and bitter fruit"?
options: A heart turning away from God to serve other gods
questions.correctAnswer: A heart turning away from God to serve other gods
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:18 (ESV): "...Beware lest there be among you a root bearing poisonous and bitter fruit..."

questions.question: With whom is the covenant made (besides those present)?
options: With him who is not here with us today (future generations)
questions.correctAnswer: With him who is not here with us today (future generations)
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:15 (ESV): "...but also with him who is not here with us today."

questions.question: Comparing the covenant in Moab to Horeb, how are they related?
options: It is beside (in addition to) the covenant made at Horeb
questions.correctAnswer: It is beside (in addition to) the covenant made at Horeb
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:1 (ESV): "...besides the covenant that he made with them at Horeb."

questions.question: What did God not give them up to this day?
options: A heart to understand or eyes to see or ears to hear
questions.correctAnswer: A heart to understand or eyes to see or ears to hear
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:4 (ESV): "But to this day the Lord has not given you a heart to understand or eyes to see or ears to hear."

questions.question: What did they not drink in the wilderness?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:6 (ESV): "You have not eaten bread, and you have not drunk wine or strong drink..."

questions.question: What false security might the wicked man have?
options: "I shall be safe, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart"
questions.correctAnswer: "I shall be safe, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart"
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 29:19 (ESV): "...he blesses himself in his heart, saying, 'I shall be safe, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart.'"

key_verse_text: The secret things belong to the LORD our God, but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children forever, that we may do all the words of this law. (ESV)
